key_inputs: Core poll weights: Datafolha 27%, Quaest 24%, AtlasIntel/Bloomberg 20%, CNT/MDA 15%, Nexus/BTG 6%, Futura 5%, Veritá 3%; their published valid-vote figures give Flávio approximately 50.9% before judgmental adjustments.

Datafolha and Quaest interviewed through 24 October, with samples of 4,050 and 3,702; Atlas interviewed 18–23 October with 4,990 respondents, while CNT/MDA interviewed 21–23 October with approximately 2,000 respondents.

Veritá's automated sample of 15,554 does not justify dominant weight; published valid-vote figures take precedence over inconsistent saved total-vote columns, and sponsor labels alone receive no directional adjustment.

The 2026 first-round two-finalist errors understated Flávio by 2.23 points at Datafolha, 2.29 at Quaest, 2.61 at Atlas and 4.16 at CNT/MDA; these errors are only partially carried forward because runoff polling can recalibrate and the electorate's choices change.

In 2022, published valid-vote estimates understated Bolsonaro by approximately 1.1 points at Datafolha and Quaest, 2.5 at Atlas and 0.2 at CNT/MDA; Futura and Veritá instead overstated him by approximately 1.2 and 1.9 points, while Datafolha's 2018 underestimate was only 0.13 point.

Flávio's first-round 47.03% against Lula's 45.16% implies approximately 51.01% among the finalists; Cury, Caiado and Zema, collectively holding 5.34% of first-round valid votes, endorsed Flávio, without guaranteeing their voters' transfers.

Datafolha's high-propensity group comprised 76% of respondents and favored Flávio 52–48, versus 48–52 among the remainder; this supports a modest turnout adjustment, not treating 76% as a turnout forecast.

First-round turnout was 78.92% and blank/null ballots were 4.77%; runoff turnout changes were −0.97 point in 2018 and +0.36 in 2022, while blank/null changes were +0.78 and +0.18 point; current CNT/MDA blank/null intentions were 5.8%.

The reported Polymarket win probability of 77% supports the direction and approximate confidence of the forecast, but its intraday timestamp is unavailable and it is not independent of polling information.

notes: The weighted core of recent polls puts Flávio near 50.9% of valid votes, emphasizing established pollsters while limiting the influence of automated sample size alone. I add approximately 0.9 point overall for partially persistent polling error and his voting-propensity advantage, substantially shrinking first-round misses and allowing historical house effects to change direction. His first-round lead and endorsements reinforce the edge, while Lula's late mobilization, social benefits and workweek proposals preserve a credible path to victory. The 80% ranges retain several points of shared polling uncertainty rather than treating polls as independent samples, and the 77% market quotation serves only as a cross-check. Turnout and blank/null estimates are anchored to the current first round and contrasting 2018/2022 runoff changes, with CNT/MDA's invalid-ballot intentions providing a secondary check.
